title: BH-01 Phase 4 browser host loader, lifecycle, and deployment gate

normalization.subject: actual-browser network capture
normalization.method: Replace random browser-generated blob UUIDs with one typed runtime-worker identity and deduplicate exact repeated request/response observations while preserving path, method, status, MIME, and cache policy.

normalization.subject: browser lifecycle capture
normalization.method: Remove nondeterministic cleanup duration and cumulative duplicate event histories while preserving outcomes, generations, resource counts, failure counts, canonical transition sequences, source-capture hash, and source byte size.

normalization.subject: profile artifact observations
normalization.method: Join observed response byte counts and cache policy to the already verified profile manifest's exact SHA-256, MIME, and profile owner; no artifact bytes are normalized.

limitations: Only one exact headless Chromium 152/Linux x86-64 environment was executed; all browsers remain unsupported.
No DOM, component, form, renderer, accessibility, LiveView, LocalLiveView, authenticated command, or server-authority behavior is established.
Popcorn 0.3.3 requires CSP unsafe-eval for tracked JavaScript execution; no production security disposition exists.
The unpruned AVM and runtime artifacts have not passed payload, startup, memory, CPU, interaction, reliability, or mobile budgets.
Reverse proxy, CDN, precompression, service worker, production HTTPS, deployment rollback, and non-local origins remain unverified.
Browser process termination cannot emit an in-page terminal cleanup record; explicit stop, pagehide/reload, failure, and context closure are covered.
The JavaScript bridge and browser profile remain experimental implementation boundaries, not stable BlazeX host or component APIs.
Cross-browser fallback, accessible messaging, constrained mobile behavior, stress, and final independent reconstruction remain later BH-01 work.

outcome.summary: Phase 4 browser-host gate passed narrowly; Phase 5 is eligible but not authorized.
outcome.expected: The governed Phoenix profile loads the exact runtime and AVM in the qualified browser, reaches observable application readiness, crosses a bounded Elixir bridge, repeats and tears down deterministically, fails intentionally for missing prerequisites and corrupt/network inputs, and accounts for every browser artifact and request without promoting support.
outcome.observed: Chrome for Testing 152 reached ready for cold, generations 2 and 3, and warm-navigation activations; each ready activation completed the Elixir echo; four stops converged to zero owned resources; missing isolation selected unsupported fallback; network and digest failures stopped intentionally; 18 files, ETag, range, MIME, cache, hash, source-map, and network-path checks passed.
